source_cards.title: Efficient synthesis of large room impulse responses in the modal domain
findings: sub-band PolyMAX/LSCF with stabilisation diagrams and pole-residue least-squares
synthetic 100-mode test recovered 95 stable poles; typical frequency error below 0.1 percent and decay/shape deviations within 2 percent
measured RIRs from three halls fitted from 20 Hz to 12 kHz with 9072, 11475 and 52470 modes
post-response ringing from spurious modes; smoothing decay times reduces ringing but shifts early-decay phase
reported real-time synthesis of 20000 modes under 15 percent of one M2 CPU core
limitations: fits individual RIRs rather than validating spatial interpolation
one highlighted source-receiver pair per hall
no listener test or held-out positions
no aggregate reconstruction-error table or confidence intervals
CPU result is hardware and implementation specific

source_cards.title: Auralization based on multi-perspective ambisonic room impulse responses
findings: matches direct sound and selected early reflections to common events before interpolation
19 experienced listeners participated; one unreliable response set excluded
plain distance-weighted linear interpolation rated below correspondence-aware variants for static localization and coloration at p below 0.001
direct sound plus ten early reflections outperformed direct sound alone for static coloration at p below 0.001
full method approached simulated reference for dynamic coloration smoothness
limitations: one measured room and one simulated room
speech and pink noise rather than a rock multitrack
Ambisonic event geometry rather than modal-pole clustering
paper-specific numeric settings are not production presets
paper licence does not itself grant implementation patent rights

metadata_only_candidates.title: On the relationship between objective room acoustic parameters and perceived differences in spatially interpolated RIRs
metadata_only_candidates.blocker: publisher full text returned access error

knowledge_cards.claim: Accurate fitting and resynthesis of individual RIRs does not validate spatial interpolation between positions.
Independent Ambisonic evidence supports direct/event correspondence before interpolation only at the general-principle level, not as replication of Bunkervik modal clustering.
Reconstruction and CPU metrics are not listener or mix-quality evidence.
Grid spacing, event count, update size, late boundary and stability thresholds are method-specific values, not transferable presets.

candidate_rules.name: correspondence_aware_rir_interpolation_shadow_only
candidate_rules.when: approved local renderer interpolates a licensed grid of measured or simulated RIR/ARIR positions
candidate_rules.change: compare explicit direct-arrival/event/mode correspondence against otherwise identical naive interpolation
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: none transferable; reviewed numeric values are method and dataset specific

experiments.question: Does direct-arrival time alignment before interpolation reduce coloration and instability relative to naive interpolation on the same RIR triplet?
experiments.material: legally reusable multi-position RIR/ARIR dataset plus fixed transient-rich music and pink-noise probes
experiments.A: distance-weighted linear interpolation of same three RIRs without direct-arrival alignment
experiments.B: identical interpolation after direct-arrival TOA alignment; no early-reflection matching or residual extrapolation
experiments.loudness: retain raw renders and create separate BS.1770-matched listening copies
experiments.listening: randomized A/B; static and slow-path conditions separate; three Dmitry repeats per probe
experiments.success: same variant wins at least two of three trials for coloration stability without protected regression
blockers: dataset and stimulus licences not audited
NEMUS Bunkervik binary excluded by EULA

references.note: No new multitrack or Reference Card.
